message: Ahoy!
Once the magic had worn off, you were able to leave the island again.
Ahoy!
The ship is still abandoned.
Silence.

replies.text: Maybe I should give that Circe another visit.

message: Ahoy!
I and my men go ashore and replenish supplies on the island. See you later.
It is rather impolite to want to steal from a friendly, weak woman.
Ahoy!
Ahoy $playername! Have you brought us a fine roast? What a splendid fellow!
Ahoy!
Hey, little landlubber - everything alright?
I wonder how much mead they have here.
Oink oink.
Oh. A guest. How unusual.

replies.text: I wasn't expecting anybody to be living on this island.

message: Few expect. Fewer ask.
I am called Circe.

replies.text: Pleased to meet you, my name is $playername.

message: Hrnnk!
Careful. They bruise easily.
They keep me company. Men are noisy. Pigs are honest.
Another pig squeals loudly.
Yes, yes. You were a sailor once. We've all made mistakes.

replies.text: Eh... well. I better leave now. Good day.

message: Enjoy the island.
You again. Did you forget something?
Crews are overrated nowadays.
The pigs shuffle. One particularly round pig freezes.
[pleasantly] Captain... who?

replies.text: He came ashore. With all his men. They vanished. You have pigs.

message: Coincidence is a powerful force.
HRNNK! HRRNNK! HRAAANK!
It stamps its hoof, glares at Circe, then at you.
Snort! Hrnnk! Oink!
It attempts a salute. Falls sideways.
SQUEE!

replies.text: That's definitely him. Turn them back.

message: Why? They seem well suited.
HRNNK!

replies.text: Looks like he says no. Change them back - NOW!

message: [Admiring] You noticed. Most would have left. Most would not have looked twice at a pig.
Pause. Circe smiles slightly.
Very well. [She murmured something.]
And another thing, you curly-tailed tyrannesse...
Why am I not pink anymore? [He looks at his hands.]
Oh thank the tides.
I remember mud. And apples. So many delicious apples.
$playername - you are observant. And inconvenient.
[She produces a small golden key.] Take this.
Not yet, not yet. When you find the lock, you will know.
Welcome, $playername.
You will not stay long. Men rarely do.
Then listen before you go.
To the southeast lie the lands of the cyclops.
They are not like other folk. They build no cities. They obey no laws but their own temper.
Each one rules his cave as if it were a kingdom.
They are strong. Suspicious. And very certain of themselves.
[slight smile] They believe they are always the larger mind in the room. That makes bargaining... difficult.
Further on you will reach a narrow strait. On one side dwells Scylla.
Scylla does not chase ships. She does not roar warnings. She simply reaches.
Six heads. Six mouths. Six chances to lose someone or something.
And what she takes, she keeps.
Do not challenge her. Do not delay near her rock. Sail past, and accept the loss she takes.
[she meets your eyes] Scylla is not cruel. She is simply hungry.
And you might meet Charybdis.

replies.text: Yes, we have met her indeed.

message: She is no creature of claw or tooth. She is hunger in the lake.
Three times each day, the waters descend into her throat. Three times they rise again.
Ships caught too near are pulled under - not smashed, but taken.
She hesitates.
Where they go, I cannot say. Some say downward. Some say elsewhere.
I have never known a sailor who returned the same.
[quietly] Or returned at all.
Sounds promising.
You cannot avoid Scylla. Charybdis or the cyclops are your choice.
With Charybdis - I wouldn't trust her, you may lose everything.
The cyclops - well, they don't like me. And the feeling is mutual.
You survived me. That suggests you prefer thought over force. You will need that.
The lake ahead does not hate you. It does not love you either.
It simply waits.
We should leave now.
The door to the cave is securely locked.
The mirror blurs. It obviously rejects you.
Baaah.
Baaah.

replies.text: You look strong enough to carry me. I hang down beneath you, and you pull me outwards.

message: The sheep carries you willingly.
Serve yourself, take all you like!

replies.text: I will take some fresh toasted bread.
Let's enjoy a whole bunch of sweet grapes.
I will sip a tiny glass of that ruby wine.

message: I love to see you growing! You may refresh yourself as long as you wish.

replies.text: I think I'll take some more...
Great! It is a wonderful place here!

message: You don't want to leave this paradise island.

replies.text: I don't want to leave this paradise island.

message: Take as much as you need.
You may leave whenever you wish.
But if you face storms or monsters tomorrow, you might prefer to do so at your strongest.
[points to the table] One grape is a courtesy. A meal is preparation.
Oh. A traveler.
[examines you carefully] You look capable. But not rested.

replies.text: In fact I seldom really am.

message: I host those who pass through. You are free to come and go as you please.
Kalypso picks a single grape from the plate.
These grow only here. The soil is... unusual.
Try one. If you dislike it, I shall be offended for exactly three seconds.
It is not enchanted wine. Not a vow. No chain.
It's just fruit.

replies.text: I might have a closer look at it.

message: [slightly amused] You may inspect it if that makes you feel heroic.
[watches intensely] Ah. You feel it, don't you?
As a token of my friendship, I give you this tiny green key.
Keep it safe. You'll know when you can use it.
The island rewards those who survive long enough to reach it.
[Her eyes flashing] Muscles awakened. Breath deepens. Old fatigue loosens its grip.
[Honest admiration] It suits you.
Now have a look at yourself how you have evolved!
You felt it.
[She does not smile] The island does not stop your feet.
It stops your wanting.
You can walk to the shore. You can touch the ship. You can even set a hand on the oar.
[softly] But your body does not wish to leave.
Yes.
The fruit strengthens what is already there.
Muscle. Breath. Certainty.
Kalypso looks at you carefully.
And it quiets the part of you that is always preparing to suffer again.
Tell me... Did you feel threatened?
I did not chain you. I did not cast a spell of obedience.
People think I imprison sailors.
I do not.
They simply discover they are tired of striving.
[A faint, almost sad smile.] Strength without struggle is very comfortable.
You wait.
[Calmly] The island's gift fades. Perfection is not meant to be permanent.
When you feel hunger again, when you feel lack again...
You will walk onto that ship without resistance.
$playername - you are free. You always were.
Hello, child. Sit down, you may keep me company.

replies.text: I have beeswax with me now.
We have a problem, sir. There's a rocky reef that the captain doesn't want to sail past. He's afraid of some singing creatures.
I have found all the new parts for your map.
I have found some of the new parts for your map.

message: Oh, really? We have sirens here in the lake? Fascinating!
Of course! Everyone with a bit of education knows about them.
However, no one has yet returned alive to report what they sing - if that's what they do.

replies.text: Then my trip is already over.

message: No, of course not. Just put something into your ears. Wax should work. Do you have beeswax with you?
You can get the best beeswax directly from a beekeeper. I know one: Leofric, I would trust him.

replies.text: Leofric? Where can I find him?
Oh, that guy. I remember him.

message: Beeswax? From Leofric I hope. Good, give it to me. I can create earplugs for you.
When he isn't out and about, he's at his bee meadow behind the Foaming Flask - in case you know it, kid.

replies.text: A rather crowded and noisy place.

message: You need one piece of wax for each pair of earplugs. So, four in total - for yourself, and for the crew.
With practiced movements, Thyrope made several pairs of earplugs.
Here, take these earplugs. The wax was perfect for them, they'll work well.

replies.text: Thank you. I'm going to go and try them out right away.

message: Good, good. Then off you go - the ship is waiting!
I am Thyrope Splathershed, the famous scholar and cartographer.

replies.text: Splathershed? Haven't I heard that name before?

message: A map maker.

replies.text: Then you must travel a lot. Have you seen my brother Andor?

message: You probably know my brother, who wrote the famous treatise on the history of Dhayavar.

replies.text: Maybe. What are you doing here?
Talking of brothers - have you seen my brother Andor?

message: Probably not. I mainly focus on the environment so I can create the most accurate maps possible.
There's less and less terra incognita... sorry, children don't understand these technical terms - I mean unknown parts of the world. My work is getting more and more difficult.
Here in Remgard, I've struck gold. The great lake here is well known in the coastal regions - but what's in the lake itself?
That's what I want to find out, and then I'll become famous with my map of the great lake.

replies.text: So you want to charter a ship and explore the lake? Sounds exciting.

message: What? No, absolutely not!
I'm not allowed to go myself. It would be an immeasurable loss to humanity if something were to happen to me.
But I'm looking for someone to make the trip and tell me about it.
You look like you don't have anything better to do right now anyway. Will you make the trip for me?

replies.text: [muttering] Nothing to do? If you only knew...

message: The ship is ready to depart from the dock, and the passage has already been paid for.
So then, Captain Burry will greet you on board!
Ohh, I'm almost dying to have the entire map complete.
Really!! That fast? I am extremely impressed. And delighted!
You talk of how you nearly got stuck at Kalypso on a paradise island.
You explain how you passed by the sirens.
You talk of the captain and his crew being turned into pigs.
You talk of blinded cyclops and sheep.
And how the six-headed monster Scylla had attacked your ship.
And finally, you raved about the gloomy land beneath the lake. What it was like to be swept into the abyss with the ship, and then to resurface again.
Thyrope Splathershed didn't seem entirely sure whether to believe your incredible story.
Thank you so much for these extremely entertaining experiences. Perhaps I'll write a story about them sometime.
As a reward you can use Captain Burry and his ship whenever you want. I will pay for it.

It swirls around you, faster and faster, until everything is black.
You wake up in a daze. The ship survived the maelstrom!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
The ship has made it back up again!
Hey! A round of mead for everyone! We sailed the entire lake!
Come closer, $playername, and learn the truth of every road you have walked and every lie told about it.
We know the names you forgot, the faces you left behind, and the fate waiting at your door.
Stay, and we will sing you the ending of your story.
No man has sailed past us unchanged, for knowledge always takes its price.
Listen, and you will understand why your brother still feels farther away with every mile.
Untie yourself, clever one - wisdom should never be heard from a distance.
What you seek is not safety, but certainty, and we can give you that.
You have outwitted monsters and men, but you have never dared to face the truth we sing.
Hear us, and you will finally know which of your victories were earned, and which were merely spared.
We sing not to trap you, $playername, but to show you what you have been running from.
One day, the knots won't be tied tightly enough. Or the blocked ears won't be closed tightly enough.
We are hungry but patient.
End of journey. This is as far as we can go.

replies.text: Hey, there is still so much to explore.

message: See the rocky island over there? This is where the sirens live.
Dreadful creatures. They have lured many a brave crew to the rocks. The ships were wrecked there, and the crew was never seen again.

replies.text: Hmm, then just ignore it and we'll drive by really quickly.

message: Absolutely not. I will not sacrifice my ship and crew to the childish wish of a kid.

replies.text: Let me think: If you didn't hear the sirens, everything would be OK, right?

message: Of course. But we can't cover our ears and steer a ship at the same time.

replies.text: Look, I have earplugs here, take them and you can drive through here as often as you like without any problems.
Look, I have earplugs here, take them and you can drive through here as often as you like without any problems.
Remember the earplugs I have given you. Use them to drive through here as often as you like without any problems.

message: Sounds like a plan. And you? How do you plan to stop yourself from simply jumping overboard?

replies.text: I'll take earplugs too, of course.
Just tie me to the mast. And whatever you do, don't untie me, no matter how much I beg.

message: Sounds like a plan. But we need a total of 4 pairs.

replies.text: Oh. Then let's turn back once more.

That's what we'll do. We'll be the first to cross the Sirens' Passage alive.

replies.text: And I am very curious to know what the sirens are shouting that lured so many to their doom.

message: You have to tell me later. And I’ll keep your pair of earplugs safe for you, just in case.
And I’ll keep your pair of earplugs safe for you, just in case.
Hello kid. Finally, a sober tavern patron!

replies.text: Yes, the noise in here is almost unbearable.

message: That's why I have produced these earplugs from beeswax. I could sell you some of them.

replies.text: With pleasure. I'd need 4 pairs for me and the crew. Show me what you have for sale.

message: Ah. Good. Nice. Home.
[sniffs] Hm. The cave smells... strange today.
Oh, a guest! How unusual.
Don't be alarmed. I'm not alarmed by myself either.
[looking in the mirror] I just look dangerous.
[to the sheep] Quiet now. The visitor is looking.
You're in luck, little one. It's not a holiday today.
[grins proudly] But it will be soon.
The door is locked. You can't leave now. Don't be angry. Rules are rules.

This door has no key. Keys always get lost... 
It only opens when I look in this mirror. Clever, clever - just like me.

replies.text: So I can't just kill you to get out again.

message: What? How you dare? Me the mightiest of all cyclops! Me Polyphem!
[beats his chest] My relatives will be coming for the next feast.
My hungry brothers.
[leans toward the player] And I'll bring the main course.
[straightens up, smugly] You can stay until then. The sheep are nice. They don't talk much.
You should take a leaf out of their book.
[turns to the mirror, straightens up] Me too, by the way. Nice, I mean. Very nice, in fact.
They say I have an eye for guests.
Who are you, anyway?
Nobody, huh? But that's not important. I just need to know what to call the dish.
Without another word, Polyphem falls onto his bed and immediately begins to snore loudly.
Hmmm? [Polyphem opens his eye for a brief moment.]
Hmmm? [Polyphem opens his eye for a brief moment, but long enough for you.]

message: It's a good thing sheep are so easy to distinguish from humans.
HA! Are you trying to sneak your way through here acting like a sheep?!

replies.text: Does it really catch the eye?

message: My favorite sheep! Your bleating sounds a bit unusual today. But I recognize you among hundreds by your wool.
Hop, hop, run outside and enjoy the delicious grass.
Baaaaah!

replies.text: Thanks, that worked out perfectly! But just to be on the safe side, carry me all the way to the ship.

message: I'd better not go into the cave. No sheep will save me again.
AAAAH - MY EYE!
MY GOOD EYE!
[staggers backward, flailing blindly] That burns!
That's cheating!
[angry] YOU! Little one! WHERE ARE YOU?!
Calm down. Stay calm.
I'll see you again in a minute.
I CAN'T SEE ANYTHING ANYMORE!
[yells outside] BROTHERS! HELP!
[bangs against the cave wall] HELP! I'VE BEEN BLINDED!
[voices from outside, muffled, bored] What's wrong, Polyphem?
NOBODY! NOBODY BLINDED ME!

... What?
If nobody blinded you, why are you screaming?
BECAUSE IT HURTS!
[desperately] NOBODY WAS DOING IT!
HE'S STANDING HERE! OR WAS STANDING! NOT ANYMORE!

COME BACK!
HE'S DANGEROUS!

Coward! Invisible coward!
[sniffs] I can still smell you.

I'll let the sheep out, then I'll find you more easily.
Don't go yet, you haven't thoroughly explored the cave.

replies.text: Well, it has worked with your brother.

message: Now let go of the ram and act like a man, kid.

BOOM!
